arabic: طَلَبَ الْوَلَدُ شِرَاءَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَحَفْنَةٍ مِنَ التُّوتِ لِلْعَشَاءِ فَقَطْ.
english: The boy asked to buy only butter and a handful of mulberries for dinner.
reason: Plausible, grammatical sentence about a boy asking to buy butter and mulberries.

arabic: هَلْ شَمُّ الزَّيْتِ الْمَغْشُوشِ إِجْرَاءٌ ضَرُورِيٌّ فِي هَذِهِ التَّجْرِبَةِ أَيْضًا؟
english: Is smelling the adulterated oil also a necessary procedure in this experiment?
reason: Smelling adulterated oil as a necessary procedure in an experiment with 'also' is a forced, contrived scenario.

arabic: الْمُحْتَوَى فِي هَذَا الْمَوْقِعِ مُتَخَصِّصٌ فِي مَجَالِ رِعَايَةِ الطُّيُورِ.
english: The content on this website specializes in bird care.
reason: Natural description of a website's content; grammatical and accurate.

arabic: هَدَفَ الْقَاضِي إِلَى إِيقَافِ الصِّرَاعِ الَّذِي انْدَلَعَ فِي الْبَلْدَةِ.
english: The judge aimed to stop the conflict that had erupted in the town.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; a judge aiming to stop a conflict is fine (though a judge mediating is slightly unusual, it works).

arabic: لَمْ يَحْكُمْ الْقَاضِي فِي الْجُنْحَةِ لِكَثْرَةِ الِاعْتِرَاضِ عَلَى الشَّهَادَةِ.
english: The judge did not rule on the misdemeanor because of the many objections to the testimony.
reason: Coherent legal sentence; grammatical and accurate. Minor: 'لم يحكمْ' is fine.

arabic: صَعِدَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى سَطْحِ الْعِمَارَةِ وَدَهِشَ مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الشِّهَابِ.
english: The boy climbed onto the building’s roof and was astonished by the meteor’s brightness.
reason: Plausible scene; grammar and translation correct.

arabic: الْوَلَدُ اللَّهِمُ ابْتَلَعَ الْقَطَائِفَ الْمَالِحَةَ، وَلَمْ يَسْتَعْمِلِ الشَّوْكَةَ فِي الْعَشَاءِ.
english: The gluttonous boy gobbled down the savory qatayef and did not use his fork at dinner.
reason: 'اللَّهِم' is an odd/rare word for gluttonous, and 'salty qatayef' is an implausible combination (qatayef are sweet), so the sentence feels forced.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ الْمُرَاهِقُ الْبَائِسُ مِنْ حَظِّهِ، وَلَمْ يَأْمَلْ فِي التَّوْفِيقِ.
english: The miserable adolescent complained about his luck and had no hope of success.
reason: Grammatical and coherent; plausible sentence.

arabic: هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةُ مُمْتِعَةٌ وَمُؤَثِّرَةٌ جِدًّا، وَقَدْ أَنْهَيْتُهَا عَلَى مَهَلٍ.
english: This story is very enjoyable and moving, and I finished it at a leisurely pace.
reason: Natural sentence; 'على مهل' means at a leisurely pace; correct.

arabic: وَقَعَ طَائِرٌ فِي الشَّبَكَةِ، فَحَنَا الْوَلَدُ رَأْسَهُ وَنَجَّاهُ مِنْهَا.
english: A bird fell into the net, so the boy bent his head down and rescued it.
reason: Bending his head to rescue a bird from a net is illogical; one would bend the body or use hands, so it's forced from a word list.

arabic: نَذَرَ الْعَامِلُ جَلْبَ حِذَاءٍ مَجَّانِيٍّ لِكُلِّ وَلَدٍ فِي الْبَلْدَةِ.
english: The worker pledged to bring free footwear for every boy in the town.
reason: A worker vowing to bring free shoes to every boy in town is an implausible scenario, and 'نذر' with a worker as the subject is forced.

arabic: غَيَّمَ النَّهَارُ فَجْأَةً وَبَرَقَ، ثُمَّ انْصَبَّ الْمَطَرُ بِضَرَاوَةٍ عَلَى الْبَلْدَةِ.
english: The day suddenly clouded over and lightning flashed, then rain poured fiercely onto the town.
reason: Natural weather description; grammatical and accurate.

arabic: اِسْتَعَانَ الْمِعْمَارُ السُّورِيُّ بِزَمِيلٍ لِتَحْدِيدِ مَقَرِّ الْبَنْكِ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
english: The Syrian architect sought a colleague’s help in determining the bank’s headquarters in this city.
reason: Grammatical and plausible. المعمار is a bit unusual for 'architect' (usually مهندس معماري) but acceptable.

arabic: النَّادِلُ الْحَبَشِيُّ خَلَطَ الْفُولَ، ثُمَّ أَضَافَ الْمِلْحَ إِلَى الصَّحْنِ.
english: The Ethiopian waiter mixed the fava beans, then added salt to the dish.
reason: Coherent scene. الحبشي is a somewhat dated word for Ethiopian, but it is acceptable. 'Mixed the fava beans, then added salt' is plausible.

arabic: فِي الْجَرَاجِ آلَةٌ مُعَقَّدَةٌ، وَهِيَ مِنْ صِنَاعَةِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
english: There is a complex machine in the garage, and it was manufactured in this city.
reason: Grammatical and plausible. الجراج means garage, and the machine is said to be made in this city.

arabic: هَلِ اسْتَحَقَّ الْمُدَرِّبُ الْأَجْنَبِيُّ هَذَا الْعِقَابَ الْقَاسِيَ عَلَى فَشَلِهِ فِي التَّمْرِينِ؟
english: Did the foreign coach deserve this harsh punishment for his failure in training?
reason: Natural rhetorical question; grammar and translation are correct.

arabic: لَمْ يَشْفِ الطِّبُّ حَنْجَرَةَ الْمُغَنِّي، وَقَدْ تَعِبَ مِنَ الْمُعَالَجَةِ.
english: Medicine has not healed the singer’s throat, and he has grown tired of treatment.
reason: Grammatical. 'Medicine has not healed the singer's throat' is plausible, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: كَانَ ذَنَبُ السِّنْجَابِ مَبْلُولًا، فَمَسَحَهُ الْمُتَطَوِّعُ الَّذِي أَنْقَذَهُ مِنَ الْقِطَّةِ.
english: The squirrel’s tail was wet, so the volunteer who rescued it from the cat wiped it.
reason: Coherent story sentence with correct grammar. ذنب is a valid word for tail, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: إِنَّ إِنْشَاءَ هَذَا الْمَتْحَفِ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَوْفِيرِ سَبْعِينَ مِلْيُونًا.
english: Building this museum requires securing seventy million.
reason: Grammatical and plausible. The currency is unspecified but this is normal in context.

arabic: هَاتِ الْمِضْرَبَ، فَهَذَا الْمَقَاسُ مُلَائِمٌ لِأَحْمَدَ فِي هَذَا التَّمْرِينِ.
english: Give me the racket; this size suits Ahmed for this exercise.
reason: Imperative هات is colloquial but fine. Racket size suiting someone is plausible.

arabic: لَيْسَ الْقَمْعُ مَبْدَأً حَضَارِيًّا، لَكِنَّ هَذِهِ الْحُكُومَةَ لَا تَزَالُ تَدْعَمُهُ.
english: Repression is not a civilized principle, but this government continues to support it.
reason: The grammar is fine, but حضاري is the correct spelling, and the contrast 'not civilized, but government still supports it' is awkward. The spelling حَضَارِيًّا with a fatha is wrong; it should be حَضَارِيًّا/حَضَارِيّ, so the form is dubious. Rejected as a borderline case.

arabic: بَاحَ أَحْمَدُ لِزَمِيلِهِ بِذِكْرَى مُؤْلِمَةٍ، ثُمَّ صَمَتَ مِنَ الْخَجَلِ.
english: Ahmed shared a painful memory with his colleague, then fell silent out of embarrassment.
reason: Natural, grammatical, and accurately translated.

arabic: مِنْ مَسَافَةٍ بَعِيدَةٍ قَدِمَ الدَّلِيلُ النُّرْوِيجِيُّ لِوَصْفِ هَذِهِ الْآثَارِ التَّارِيخِيَّةِ.
english: The Norwegian guide came from far away to describe these historical monuments.
reason: Plausible, grammatical sentence with correct fronting of the prepositional phrase.

arabic: أَحْمَدُ هَمَسَ بِسُرُورٍ لِزَمِيلِهِ: «رَضِيَ الْمَالِكُ عَنْ ذَوْقِكَ فِي الْفَرْشِ».
english: Ahmed whispered happily to his colleague: “The owner was pleased with your taste in furnishings.”
reason: Plausible dialogue. رضي عن is correct, and الفرش means furnishings.

arabic: أَدْرُسُ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ وَنُطْقَ حُرُوفِ الْأَبْجَدِيَّةِ بِجِدٍّ فِي هَذَا الْمَرْكَزِ.
english: I diligently study phonetics and the pronunciation of alphabet letters at this center.
reason: Grammatical and plausible: studying phonetics and letter pronunciation at a center.

arabic: الْمُصَوِّرُ نَظَّمَ مَجْمُوعَةَ صُوَرٍ عَنِ الطَّبِيعَةِ فِي النِّرْوِيجِ لِلْمِهْرَجَانِ.
english: The photographer organized a collection of photographs about nature in Norway for the festival.
reason: Fluent, plausible sentence about a photographer preparing a photo collection for a festival.

arabic: قِيَاسُ هَذِهِ الْبِذْلَةِ مُتَوَسِّطٌ، وَحَجْمُهَا يُنَاسِبُ صَاحِبَ هَذَا الدُّكَّانِ جِدًّا.
english: This suit is medium-sized, and its size suits the owner of this shop very well.
reason: Odd: a suit's size suiting a shop owner 'very well' is a forced combination, and بذلة/قياس/حجم redundancy makes it unnatural.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَجَاهَلْ عُضْوُ الْمُؤَسَّسَةِ شُحُوبَ الْجَرِيحِ، فَفَحَصَهُ الْمُمَرِّضُ فِي هَذَا الْمَرْكَزِ.
english: The institution's member did not ignore the injured person's pallor, so the nurse examined him at this center.
reason: Forced word-list sentence: 'institution's member' is awkward, and the causal link between ignoring pallor and the nurse at a center is contrived.

arabic: هَلْ دَامَتْ مُعَانَاةُ الْجَرِيحِ نِصْفَ شَهْرٍ فِي هَذَا السِّجْنِ؟
english: Did the injured person's suffering last half a month in this prison?
reason: An injured person's suffering in a prison for half a month is a contrived combination; the scenario is incoherent without hidden context.

arabic: أَطْعَمَ الْجَارُ الْعِجْلَ الْجَوْعَانَ، ثُمَّ دَاعَبَهُ فِي سَاحَةِ الْمَطْحَنَةِ.
english: The neighbor fed the hungry calf, then petted it in the mill's courtyard.
reason: Coherent rural scene: neighbor feeds a hungry calf and plays with it in the mill courtyard.

arabic: أَلْقَى صَاحِبُ الدُّكَّانِ الْمِقَصَّ وَالْمُشْطَ فِي مُؤَخَّرَةِ هَذَا الدُّولَابِ.
english: The shop owner tossed the scissors and comb into the back of this cupboard.
reason: Tossing scissors and comb into the back of a cupboard is odd and forced; also مِقَصّ with مشط is a random pairing.

arabic: فِي الشَّهْرِ الْهِجْرِيِّ التَّاسِعِ، صَامَ الْجَارُ وَكَانَ مِزَاجُهُ طَيِّبًا.
english: In the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, the neighbor fasted and was in a good mood.
reason: Ninth Hijri month is Ramadan; neighbor fasting in a good mood is plausible and grammatical.

arabic: مُدَرِّبُ التَّزَلُّجِ الْمُفَضَّلُ لَدَى الْبَنَاتِ مُعْتَادٌ عَلَى اسْتِضَافَةِ الْمِهْرَجَانِ هُنَا.
english: The girls' favorite skiing coach is accustomed to hosting the festival here.
reason: Forced word-list sentence: a skiing coach favored by girls hosting a festival is incoherent.

arabic: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي هَذَا الْمُسَلْسَلِ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيِّ الْمُضْحِكِ وَتَصْنِيفِهِ الْجَدِيدِ؟
english: What do you think of this funny English series and its new classification?
reason: 'New classification' of a series is a forced addition; the sentence feels like word-list stuffing.

arabic: وَفْقًا لِهَذِهِ الْمَادَّةِ، قَبُولُ الْمَتَاعِ مَحْدُودٌ فِي هَذَا الْمَرْكَزِ.
english: According to this clause, the acceptance of baggage is limited at this center.
reason: 'Acceptance of baggage is limited at this center' is a forced combination; المادة as 'clause' is acceptable but the scene is incoherent.

arabic: تَوَلَّدَتْ ثِقَةُ النَّاسِ فِي رِئَاسَةِ الْمُؤَسَّسَةِ مِنْ نَزَاهَةِ الْقَائِدِ الْإِدَارِيِّ.
english: People's trust in the institution's leadership arose from the administrative leader's integrity.
reason: Grammatical, formal and plausible statement about trust arising from a leader's integrity.

arabic: حَرَّكَتِ الْأُمُّ خَلِيطَ الْخَضْرَاوَاتِ وَالْبَهَارِ فِي الزَّبْدِيَّةِ، ثُمَّ وَزَّعَتْهُ عَلَى الْأَصْحَابِ.
english: The mother stirred the mixture of vegetables and spices in the bowl, then served it to her friends.
reason: Arabic says distributed it to 'the friends' (الأصحاب), not 'her friends'; 'served' is OK, but the mixture of vegetables and spices stirred then distributed is plausible. Minor: 'her' is added, but acceptable. Still, 'وزعته' fits 'served'. Translation is close enough but 'her' is unsupported.

arabic: عَلَى الْمَائِدَةِ مُقَبِّلَاتٌ وَصَيَّادِيَةٌ، لَكِنَّ الضَّيْفَ مُولَعٌ بِالْمَنْسَفِ فَقَطْ.
english: There are appetizers and sayadieh on the table, but the guest is only fond of mansaf.
reason: Natural scene; 'صيادية' is a fish and rice dish, 'مولع بالمنسف' is fine. Mixing Levantine dishes is plausible.

arabic: الْهَمْسْتَرُ الْمَنْفُوشُ تَحَرَّكَ مُتَثَاقِلًا مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ إِلَى الشَّنْطَةِ الْخَاوِيَةِ.
english: The fluffy hamster moved sluggishly from the box into the empty bag.
reason: Awkward: a hamster moving 'sluggishly' from a box into an empty bag is an odd, forced scene; 'الشنطة الخاوية' is mixed register. Weak plausibility.

arabic: فِي الْعِيَادَةِ مَرِيضٌ صَبُورٌ يَتَوَقَّعُ الشِّفَاءَ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَرَضِ.
english: There is a patient man at the clinic who expects to recover from this illness.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; patient (calm) man expecting recovery. 'صبور' as 'patient' (temperament) is correctly rendered.

arabic: عَجِبَ الْأَصْحَابُ مِنْ غَرَابَةِ الْأُسْطُورَةِ وَمِنَ التَّشْوِيقِ فِي كُلِّ سُطُورِهَا.
english: The friends marveled at the strangeness of the legend and the suspense throughout its lines.
reason: Grammatical and coherent; friends marvel at the strange legend and its suspense. Slightly literary but plausible.

arabic: هَلْ فِي هَذَا الْمَطْعَمِ سَنْدَوِيتْشُ طَاوُوقٍ أَوْ هَمْبَرْجَرٌ مُزْدَوِجٌ أَيْضًا؟
english: Does this restaurant also have a tawook sandwich or a double hamburger?
reason: Natural restaurant question; tawook sandwich and double hamburger are plausible menu items. 'أو...أيضًا' is slightly redundant but acceptable.

arabic: أَضَاءَ الْقِنْدِيلُ الطَّاقَ، فَظَهَرَ بَهَاءُ الْمَبْنَى الْبِيزَنْطِيِّ فِي هَذَا الْمَشْهَدِ.
english: The lantern illuminated the arch, revealing the Byzantine building’s splendor in this scene.
reason: Descriptive literary sentence, grammatical and coherent.

arabic: الْمُمَثِّلَةُ مَبْسُوطَةٌ بِالْجِينْزِ وَالنَّظَّارَةِ الْجَدِيدَةِ لِلْمِهْرَجَانِ فِي الْجُمُعَةِ الْمُقْبِلَةِ.
english: The actress is happy with the jeans and new glasses for the festival next Friday.
reason: Awkward and forced: 'مبسوطة بالجينز والنظارة الجديدة للمهرجان' lumps items oddly, and 'في الجمعة المقبلة' is unidiomatic (should be يوم الجمعة).

arabic: أَوْشَكَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ الْمَذْعُورَةُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ دَوَّامَةً فَظِيعَةً، لَكِنَّهَا بَلَغَتِ الْبَرَّ.
english: The frightened turtle nearly entered a dreadful whirlpool, but it reached land.

arabic: لَنْ يَمْنَعَ عِنَادُ الرَّئِيسِ الْخُبَرَاءَ النَّشِيطِينَ مِنْ أَنْ يَتَشَاوَرُوا.
english: The chief’s stubbornness will not prevent the active experts from consulting together.

arabic: كَنَسَتِ الشَّغَّالَةُ فَضْلَةَ الْجُرَذِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَاعَةِ، وَدَمْدَمَتْ بِغِلٍّ.
english: The housekeeper swept the rat dropping out of this hall and muttered resentfully.
reason: Coherent scene; 'فضلة الجرذ' is plausible for rat droppings and the maid muttering resentfully is natural.

arabic: هَذَا النَّعْنَاعُ الْمَغْلِيُّ مُهَدِّئٌ، لَكِنَّ الْعِرْقْسُوسَ أَفْضَلُ لِي فِي السَّفَرِ.
english: This boiled mint is soothing, but I prefer licorice when traveling.
reason: Natural personal statement about herbal drinks; grammatical and accurate.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ الوَلَدُ لِأَنَّ شِرَاءَ الحِذَاءِ كَانَ مُتْعِبًا جِدًّا.
english: The boy complained because buying the shoes was very tiring.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; simple learner sentence.

arabic: يَرْغَبُ الرَّجُلُ النَّبَاتِيُّ فِي زُبْدَةٍ طَازَجَةٍ وَحَفْنَةٍ مِنَ التُّوتِ.
english: The vegetarian man wants some fresh butter and a handful of mulberries.
reason: Forced word-list combination; a vegetarian wanting butter and mulberries is odd, and 'vegetarian' (نباتي) with butter is a contrived scene.

arabic: انْدَلَعَ صِرَاعٌ بِضَرَاوَةٍ فِي البَلْدَةِ، فَوَقَعَ دَمَارٌ فِي عِمَارَةِ الشَّارِعِ.
english: A conflict broke out fiercely in the town, so destruction struck the street's building.
reason: 'عمارة الشارع' is awkward and the sentence is contrived; 'بضراوة' with انْدَلَعَ and the causal 'so' is forced.

arabic: المُوَاصَلَةُ مَجَّانِيَّةٌ فِي رُبْعِ البَلْدَةِ فَقَطْ، وَلِهَذَا هُنَاكَ اعْتِرَاضٌ.
english: Transportation is free in only a quarter of the town, and for this reason there is an objection.
reason: 'المواصلة' and 'ربع البلدة' (quarter as a district) are awkward; 'ربع' as a neighborhood is questionable and the sentence feels forced. 'مواصلات' would be natural.

arabic: بَرَقَ شِهَابٌ فِي مَدَارِهِ، وَكَانَ ضِيَاؤُهُ مُتَّقِدًا وَسَطَ الظَّلَامِ.
english: A meteor flashed in its orbit, and its radiance was blazing in the middle of the darkness.
reason: Poetic but grammatical and plausible description of a meteor, though 'in its orbit' is slightly odd.

arabic: خَبَرَ المُتَخَصِّصُ فِي مَجَالِ الفِيزْيَاءِ تَجْرِبَةً بِاللَّيْزَرِ، ثُمَّ أَنْهَىٰ الإِجْرَاءَ مَعَ الزُّمَلَاءِ.
english: The specialist in the field of physics tested a laser experiment, then finished the procedure with his colleagues.
reason: خَبَرَ is an odd verb for 'tested' an experiment; 'tested a laser experiment' is unnatural. 'أجرى تجربة' would be expected.

arabic: نَجَّى الرَّجُلُ الوَلَدَ الَّذِي غَرِقَ فِي الشَّلَّالِ، فَكَانَ ذَلِكَ حَظًّا وَمُعْجِزَةً حَقِيقِيَّةً.
english: The man rescued the boy who sank in the waterfall, and that was luck and a real miracle.

arabic: نَذَرَ الرَّجُلُ هُنَاكَ فِي الكَنِيسَةِ أَنْ يَعْبُدَ الإِلٰهَ آبَادًا.
english: The man vowed there in the church to worship God for ages.
reason: 'آبادًا' as 'for ages' and 'يعبد الإله' is unnatural; the vow in a church is contrived and the phrasing is awkward.

arabic: رَمَّ العَامِلُ الشَّبَكَةَ فِي الوَاحَةِ وَنَوَّعَ زِرَاعَةَ القَمْحِ وَالعِنَبِ.
english: The worker repaired the net in the oasis and diversified the cultivation of wheat and grapes.
reason: Repairing a net and diversifying wheat and grape cultivation are unrelated actions combined as a forced word list.

arabic: حَكَمَ القَاضِي بِأَنَّ بَيْعَ الزَّيْتِ المَغْشُوشِ حَرَامٌ وَضَارٌّ، وَعَاقَبَ صَاحِبَهُ.
english: The judge ruled that selling adulterated oil is forbidden and harmful, and he punished its owner.
reason: Grammatical, coherent legal statement about selling adulterated oil.

arabic: تَلَا الوَلَدُ القَافِلَةَ عَلَى مَهَلٍ، وَمَضَى الزَّمَانُ وَهُوَ صَابِرٌ.
english: The boy followed the caravan at a leisurely pace, and time passed while he stayed patient.
reason: The two clauses are disconnected, and 'تلا' for following a caravan with 'time passed' is a forced, incoherent scene.

arabic: القِصَّةُ مُؤَثِّرَةٌ سِيَّمَا لِلْوَلَدِ البَائِسِ الَّذِي هَاجَرَ مِنَ الهِنْدِ.
english: The story is moving, especially for the miserable boy who emigrated from India.
reason: 'سِيَّمَا' without 'لا' is incorrect; it should be 'لا سيما'.

arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ عُودًا طَوِيلًا فِي الْجَرَاجِ ثُمَّ هَرَبَ مِنَ الْقِطَّةِ.
english: The squirrel climbed a long piece of wood in the garage, then escaped from the cat.
reason: A squirrel climbing a 'long piece of wood' (عود) in a garage is a forced combination. عود is an odd word choice here and الجراج is awkward. Reads like a word-list sentence.

arabic: اِسْتَعَانَ الْمِعْمَارُ بِدَلِيلٍ لِتَحْدِيدِ مَسَافَةِ مَقَرِّ الْحُكُومَةِ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ.
english: The architect sought the help of a guide to determine the distance of the government headquarters in the city.
reason: 'Determine the distance of the government headquarters' is awkward. An architect hiring a guide to measure distance is implausible, and المعمار is unusual.

arabic: خَلَطَ النَّادِلُ الْحَلِيبَ بِالْمِلْحِ فَغَيَّظَ الدُّكْتُورَ وَلَمْ يَرْضَ بِالذَّوْقِ.
english: The waiter mixed the milk with salt, which angered the doctor, and he was not satisfied with the taste.
reason: The sentence is stilted. غيّظ is unnatural, and the second clause 'he was not satisfied' has an ambiguous subject. A waiter mixing milk with salt is odd.

arabic: فِي الصُّبْحِ نَفَخَ الطَّاوُوسُ ذَنَبَهُ الطَّوِيلَ فَهَرَبَتِ الْفَرَاشَةُ مِنْهُ.
english: In the morning the peacock puffed out its long tail, so the butterfly fled from it.
reason: A coherent, plausible scene. The peacock fans its tail and the butterfly flees. The grammar is fine.

arabic: تَبَادَلَ الْحَبَشِيُّ وَالسُّورِيُّ ذِكْرَى وَاحِدَةً عَنِ الْمَدِينَةِ ثُمَّ صَمَتَا.
english: The Ethiopian and the Syrian exchanged one memory about the city, then fell silent.
reason: 'Exchanged one memory about the city' is odd. The pairing of الحبشي and السوري is a forced word-list combination. الحبشي is also dated.

arabic: تَطَوَّرَ الطِّبُّ فِعْلًا وَشَمِلَ تَوْفِيرَ آلَةٍ لِلْمُعَالَجَةِ فِي الْكُوَيْتِ.
english: Medicine has really developed and now includes providing a device for treatment in Kuwait.
reason: The sentence is a vague, forced combination. 'Providing a device for treatment in Kuwait' is a catalog-like proposition, and آلة للمعالجة is unnatural.

arabic: لَيْسَ الْفَشَلُ عَيْبًا وَلَا خَجَلًا، فَلَا تَسْخَرْ مِنْ زَمِيلِكَ.
english: Failure is not a defect or a shame, so do not mock your colleague.
reason: Natural, grammatical moral advice. The translation is accurate.

arabic: لَعَلَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ يَسْتَحِقُّ السُّلْطَانَ وَالثَّرْوَةَ، لَكِنَّ الْغَازِيَ أَطَاحَ بِهِ.
english: Perhaps the caliph deserves power and wealth, but the invader overthrew him.
reason: Grammatical and plausible in a historical or narrative context. The translation is accurate.

arabic: هَذِهِ الطَّبَّاعَةُ آلَةٌ مُعَقَّدَةٌ، لَكِنَّ مَقَاسَهَا مُلَائِمٌ جِدًّا لِلشَّقَّةِ.
english: This printer is a complicated machine, but its size is very suitable for the apartment.
reason: The sentence is grammatical, but 'a printer is a complicated machine, but its size suits the apartment' is a forced combination. The printer is also called طابعة, not طباعة, which means 'printing'.

arabic: رَفَعَ الْأَجِيرُ الْعَجَلَةَ ثُمَّ مَسَحَهَا بِوِشَاحٍ رَطْبٍ فِي الْكَرَاجِ.
english: The laborer lifted the wheel, then wiped it with a damp scarf in the garage.
reason: Wiping a wheel with a damp scarf (وشاح) is implausible. A scarf is not a cleaning cloth, so the sentence is forced.

arabic: تَعِبَتِ الصَّائِمَاتُ فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ لَكِنَّ سُرُورَهُنَّ بِالصِّيَامِ بَاقٍ.
english: The fasting women grew tired in the desert, but their joy in fasting remains.
reason: Grammatical, with correct feminine plural agreement, and plausible. The translation is accurate.

arabic: دَعَمَتِ الْحُكُومَةُ إِنْشَاءَ صِنَاعَةٍ بَلَدِيَّةٍ لِتَحْسِينِ الِاقْتِصَادِ فِي الْجَنُوبِ.
english: The government supported the creation of a native industry to improve the economy in the south.

arabic: أَدْرُسُ الآنَ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ وَالأَبْجَدِيَّةَ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ وَنُطْقَ الحُرُوفِ فِي المَرْكَزِ.
english: I am now studying phonetics, the English alphabet, and the pronunciation of letters at the center.
reason: Forced word-list: phonetics, English alphabet and letter pronunciation listed together; the list feels contrived and 'phonetics' plus 'alphabet' plus 'pronunciation of letters' is redundant.

arabic: نَظَّمَ عُضْوٌ فِي رِئَاسَةِ المُؤَسَّسَةِ مِهْرَجَانًا جَدِيدًا وَفْقًا لِقَرَارِ المَجْمُوعَةِ.
english: A member of the institution's leadership organized a new festival according to the group's decision.
reason: Grammatical and plausible institutional news-style sentence; translation accurate.

arabic: تَجَاهَلَتِ السِّفَارَةُ سُؤَالَ المُصَوِّرِ عَنِ التَّأْشِيرَةِ، فَهُوَ زَعْلَانُ جِدًّا.
english: The embassy ignored the photographer's question about the visa, so he is very upset.
reason: Uses colloquial 'زعلان' in an otherwise formal MSA sentence; also the causal link is odd. Mixed register is not correct MSA.

arabic: شَاخَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ المُعَانَاةِ وَضَعُفَ، وَبَانَ الشُّحُوبُ عَلَى لِحْيَتِهِ.
english: The man aged from suffering and grew weak, and paleness showed on his beard.
reason: Literary, grammatical sentence; paleness showing on the beard is slightly unusual but acceptable as poetic/descriptive.

arabic: التَّزَلُّجُ رِيَاضَةٌ مُفَضَّلَةٌ فِي نِرْوَيج لِأَنَّ الطَّبِيعَةَ هُنَاكَ جَمِيلَةٌ.
english: Skiing is a favorite sport in Norway because the nature there is beautiful.
reason: Natural, grammatical; 'نرويج' is a standard variant spelling (النرويج usually with article), acceptable.

arabic: كَانَ حَجْمُ هَذَا الصَّرْحِ سِتِّينَ مِتْرًا فِي القِيَاسِ السَّابِقِ.
english: The size of this edifice was sixty meters in the previous measurement.
reason: Awkward: 'size' of an edifice given as sixty meters (a length/height) 'in the previous measurement' is a contrived word-list sentence.

arabic: وَحَّدَ القَائِدُ الجُنْدَ بِالجِدِّ وَالطَّاعَةِ، ثُمَّ قَادَهُمْ إِلَى النَّجَاحِ.
english: The leader unified the troops through diligence and obedience, then led them to success.
reason: Grammatical, coherent, plausible; translation accurate.

arabic: دَامَ قَبُولُ النَّاسِ لِلنَّائِبِ بِنَزَاهَتِهِ، وَلَمْ يَجِدْ عَدُوُّهُ حِيلَةً.
english: People's acceptance of the deputy endured thanks to his integrity, and his enemy found no trick.
reason: Grammatical and coherent; translation accurate.

arabic: الطِّفْلُ جَوْعَانُ جِدًّا، فَأَطْعَمَتْهُ مَامَا نِصْفَ الفُلْفُلِ المَحْشِيِّ وَالزَّيْتُونَ.
english: The child is very hungry, so Mom fed him half of the stuffed pepper and the olives.
reason: Uses colloquial 'مامّا' and mixes registers; the food combination is also contrived.

arabic: صَامَ النَّاسُ شَهْرًا هِجْرِيًّا كَامِلًا مِنْ ظُهُورِ الهِلَالِ إِلَى العِيدِ.
english: People fasted a whole Hijri month, from the appearance of the crescent until Eid.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; fasting Ramadan from crescent to Eid; translation accurate.

arabic: تَوَفَّى العَبْدُ فِي السِّجْنِ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ عَوْدَةٌ، فَقَبَرَهُ النَّاسُ هُنَاكَ.
english: The servant died in prison and had no return, so people buried him there.
reason: Odd phrasing: 'لم تكن له عودة' and burying him there with 'قبره' is awkward; 'تُوُفِّيَ' should be passive and 'توفى' as written is a grammatical problem for active form.

arabic: وَجَدَ الوَصِيفُ فِي الدُّولَابِ مُشْطًا وَمِقَصًّا وَلَزْقَةً وَبِذْلَةً جَدِيدَةً.
english: The young man found a comb, scissors, a plaster, and a new suit in the wardrobe.
reason: 'الوصيف' means a young servant/page, not just 'young man'; also 'مقص' form 'مِقَصًّا' is incorrect (should be مِقَصًّا/مِقَصّ irregular), and the list of items is a contrived word list.

arabic: أَضَاءَ القِنْدِيلُ الطَّاقَ الخَاوِيَ فِي الكَاتِدْرَائِيِّ، فَظَهَرَ بَهَاؤُهُ.
english: The lantern lit up the empty arch in the cathedral, and its splendor appeared.
reason: Grammatical and plausible descriptive sentence; slightly literary but fine. (الكاتدرائية usually with ة, but الكاتدرائي is a stretch; acceptable.)

arabic: وَاظَبَ المَرِيضُ عَلَى العِيَادَةِ، فَخَفَّفَتِ العِيَادَةُ أَلَمَ عَضَلَةِ كَتِفِهِ، وَاقْتَرَبَ الشِّفَاءُ.
english: The patient kept going to the clinic, so the clinic eased the pain of his shoulder muscle, and recovery drew near.
reason: Clinic itself easing muscle pain is odd; 'kept going to the clinic, so the clinic eased' is awkward repetition and forced word-list use.

arabic: فِي العِرْسِ اِمْتَلَأَتِ المَائِدَةُ بِالمُقَبِّلَاتِ وَالمَنْسَفِ، وَبَقِيَتْ زَبْدِيَّةُ الصَّيَّادِيَّةِ خَاوِيَةً.
english: At the wedding, the table filled up with appetizers and mansaf, and the bowl of sayadieh remained empty.
reason: Coherent wedding scene; mansaf and sayadieh are real dishes, grammar fine.

arabic: الوَلَدُ مُولَعٌ بِالهَمْبَرْجَرِ وَالسَّنْدَوِيتْشِ، لَكِنَّ أُمَّهُ تَظُنُّ أَنَّ الخَضْرَاوَاتِ أَفْضَلُ.
english: The boy is fond of hamburgers and sandwiches, but his mother thinks vegetables are better.
reason: Natural, grammatically correct sentence; translation accurate.

arabic: دَمْدَمَ القَانِصُ إِذْ أَوْشَكَ الجُرَذُ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ المَبْنَى.
english: The hunter muttered when the rat was about to enter the building.
reason: Hunter muttering because a rat nears a building is an implausible, forced scenario; القانص also an odd word choice.

arabic: تَحَرَّكَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ مُتَثَاقِلَةً، وَنَامَ الهَمْسْتَرُ المَنْفُوشُ فِي الصُّنْدُوقِ.
english: The turtle moved sluggishly, and the fluffy hamster slept in the box.
reason: Two unrelated clauses joined without coherence; a word-list combination.

arabic: ظَهَرَتِ العَزْبَاءُ فِي المِهْرَجَانِ بِجِينْزٍ وَنَظَّارَةٍ مُسْتَدِيرَةٍ، وَهِيَ مَبْسُوطَةٌ.
english: The single woman appeared at the festival in jeans and round eyeglasses, and she was happy.
reason: Plausible colloquial-tinged sentence; مبسوطة is colloquial but acceptable; translation fine.

arabic: الأُمُّ صَبُورٌ، لَكِنَّ عِنَادَ الوَلَدِ وَمَشَقَّةَ الدَّرْسِ جَعَلَاهَا مُؤَنِّبَةً.
english: The mother is patient, but the boy's stubbornness and the hardship of the lesson made her reproachful.
reason: Dual verb جعلاها is fine, but 'patient mother made reproachful' with abstract noun pair feels forced; مؤنِّبة as predicate is awkward (should be جعلاها تؤنّب).

arabic: تَوَقَّعَ الخَبِيرُ أَنْ يَكُونَ المَطَرُ أَغْزَرَ فِي الجُمْعَةِ المُقْبِلَةِ فَيَغْمُرَ البَلْدَةَ.
english: The expert expected the rain to be more abundant next Friday and flood the town.
reason: Grammatical with correct subjunctive; plausible weather forecast sentence.

arabic: النَّعْنَاعُ المَغْلِيُّ وَالعِرْقسُوسُ مُهَدِّئَانِ لِلْحَلَقِ، وَيُخَفِّفَانِ الأَلَمَ.
english: Boiled mint and licorice are soothing for the throat, and they reduce the pain.
reason: Natural statement about herbal drinks soothing the throat; grammar correct.

arabic: تَلَقَّطَتِ الشَّغَّالَةُ البَامْيَا وَالإِجَّاصَ، ثُمَّ كَسْكَسَتْ بِالبَهَارِ لِلضَّيْفِ.
english: The housemaid gathered okra and pears, then prepared couscous with spices for the guest.
reason: كسكست is not a real standard verb and 'prepared couscous with spices' is a forced interpretation; gathering okra and pears is incoherent.

arabic: تَشَاوَرَ الأَصْحَابُ فِي لُغْزِ الأُسْطُورَةِ، وَعَجِبُوا مِنْ غَرَابَةِ الخَبِيئَةِ.
english: The friends conferred about the riddle of the legend, and marveled at the strangeness of the hidden thing.
reason: 'Riddle of the legend' and 'strangeness of the hidden thing' (الخبيئة) is a forced, vague word-list combination.

arabic: الزُّبْدَةُ المَغْشُوشَةُ ضَارَّةٌ بِالقَلْبِ، وَلَا سِيَّمَا الزُّبْدَةُ المَالِحَةُ جِدًّا.
english: Adulterated butter is harmful to the heart, especially very salty butter.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ العَامِلُ البَائِسُ مِنَ العَمَلِ المُتْعِبِ فِي العِمَارَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ.
english: The miserable worker complained about the tiring work in the ninth building.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; a worker complaining about tiring work in a building. Ordinal agreement is correct.

arabic: ابْتَلَعَ الوَلَدُ اللَّهِمُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ التُّوتِ، ثُمَّ غَسَلَ شَفَتَيْهِ.
english: The greedy boy swallowed a handful of mulberries, then washed his lips.
reason: Washing his lips after eating mulberries is odd, and 'greedy boy' reads like a forced word-list combination. The sequence is contrived.

arabic: الفَتَاةُ النَّبَاتِيَّةُ رَغِبَتْ فِي عَشَاءٍ مِنَ الأَعْشَابِ الطَّازَجَةِ وَالقَمْحِ.
english: The vegetarian girl wanted a dinner of fresh herbs and wheat.

arabic: انْدَلَعَ صِرَاعٌ أَهْلِيٌّ فِي البَلْدَةِ، فَهَاجَرَ رُبْعُ العُمَّالِ إِلَى الهِنْدِ.
english: A civil conflict broke out in the town, so a quarter of the workers emigrated to India.
reason: Coherent cause and effect; grammatical. Civil conflict leading workers to emigrate is plausible.

arabic: صَعِدَ النَّمِرُ المُنْفَرِدُ إِلَى سَطْحِ الكُوخِ، فَدَهِشَ الزَّائِرُ مِنْ ضَرَاوَتِهِ.
english: The solitary tiger climbed onto the roof of the hut, and the visitor was astonished by its ferocity.
reason: A tiger climbing onto a hut roof is implausible, since tigers don't typically do this. The sentence reads as a forced word list.

arabic: أَنْهَى المُتَخَصِّصُ إِجْرَاءَاتِ التَّجْرِبَةِ الأُولَى، لَكِنَّ الحَظَّ كَانَ سَيِّئًا.
english: The specialist finished the procedures of the first experiment, but the luck was bad.
reason: 'The luck was bad' after finishing procedures is incoherent. The first clause has no real link to the second, so the sentence is forced.

arabic: حَنَا الوَلَدُ المَغْرُورُ رَأْسَهُ وَاسْتَحْيَا، لِأَنَّهُ خَالَفَ الأُسْتَاذَ فِي الحِصَّةِ.
english: The arrogant boy bowed his head and felt ashamed, because he had contradicted the teacher in class.
reason: Grammatical and natural. A boy bows his head in shame for contradicting the teacher.

arabic: خَفِيَتْ شَوْكَةٌ فِي حِذَاءِ الطِّفْلِ، فَبَسَرَ وَتَمَلْمَلَ فِي البَاصِ.
english: A thorn was hidden in the child's shoe, so he frowned and fidgeted on the bus.
reason: 'خَفِيَتْ' (was hidden) is awkward for a thorn in a shoe. 'بَسَرَ' is a rare word for frowning, and 'البَاص' is colloquial, so the register is mixed. The sentence is contrived.

arabic: وَقَعَ شِهَابٌ مُتَّقِدٌ فِي الوَاحَةِ، فَانْصَبَّ ضِيَاؤُهُ عَلَى الأَكْوَاخِ.
english: A burning meteor fell in the oasis, and its radiance poured over the huts.
reason: Grammatical and poetic or narrative. A meteor falling with light pouring over the huts is plausible in a story.

arabic: فِي ذَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ، نَذَرَ الرَّجُلُ العَجَمِيُّ كَبْشًا لِإِلٰهِهِ الَّذِي عَبَدَهُ.
english: In that age, the foreign man vowed a ram to the god he worshipped.
reason: 'العَجَمِيّ' (non-Arab/Persian) rendered as 'foreign' is loose. The sentence is also redundant and contrived ('his god whom he worshipped').

arabic: طَالَمَا كَانَ مُحْتَوَى المَوْقِعِ مَجَّانِيًّا وَمُمْتِعًا، فَسَأَتَصَفَّحُهُ عَلَى مَهَلٍ.
english: As long as the website's content is free and enjoyable, I will browse it at my leisure.
reason: Natural and grammatical. 'طالما' means 'as long as', and the future clause with 'على مهل' is idiomatic.

arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ العُودَ الرَّطْبَ عَلَى عَجَلَةٍ، وَكَانَ ذَنَبُهُ طَوِيلًا.
english: The squirrel climbed the damp wood in a hurry, and its tail was long.
reason: Squirrel climbing 'damp wood' (العود الرطب) is odd; 'on a hurry' phrasing and the tacked-on tail clause make it a forced word-list sentence. العود is also a stick/oud, not natural here.

arabic: سَعَلَ النَّادِلُ الأَجْنَبِيُّ ثُمَّ هَمَسَ، فَقَدْ تَعِبَتْ حَنْجَرَتُهُ.
english: The foreign waiter coughed and then whispered, because his throat had grown tired.
reason: Grammatical and coherent: a waiter coughs then whispers because his throat is tired.

arabic: المِعْمَارُ السُّورِيُّ أَضَافَ جَرَاجًا إِلَى مَقَرِّ الحُكُومَةِ التَّارِيخِيِّ فِي المَدِينَةِ.
english: The Syrian architect added a garage to the historic government headquarters in the city.
reason: Adding a garage to a historic government headquarters is implausible, and 'جراج' with a forced list of attributes feels contrived; grammar is fine but scenario is odd.

arabic: يَا تُرَى، هَلْ يَسْتَحِقُّ هَذَا الفَشَلُ كُلَّ هَذَا الخَجَلِ؟
english: I wonder, does this failure deserve all this shame?
reason: Natural rhetorical question using يا ترى; grammatical and accurately translated.

arabic: لَعَلَّ الطِّبَّ يَشْفِي الخَدَرَ البَاقِيَ فِي فَخِذِهِ بَعْدَ أُسْبُوعٍ.
english: Perhaps medicine will heal the numbness left in his thigh after a week.
reason: 'Medicine heals the numbness in his thigh after a week' is a forced combination; الطب as agent of شفى with لعل is unnatural.

arabic: شَحَبَتْ بَعْضُ الصَّائِمَاتِ بَعْدَ الصِّيَامِ الطَّوِيلِ، فَاسْتَعَنَّ بِدُكْتُورٍ لَطِيفٍ.
english: Some of the fasting women turned pale after the long fast, so they sought help from a kind doctor.
reason: شحبت with بعض (masculine/feminine agreement is acceptable) but the sentence is odd: fasting women turning pale and seeking a 'kind doctor' is contrived; 'استعنّ بدكتور' is also unidiomatic.

arabic: أَوْحَتْ أَلْوَانُ الفَرَاشَةِ لِلْبِنْتِ بِوَشْمٍ مُلَائِمٍ لِذَوْقِهَا عَلَى كَتِفِهَا.
english: The butterfly's colors gave the girl the idea for a tattoo on her shoulder that suited her taste.
reason: Coherent and plausible: butterfly colors inspired a girl's tattoo choice; أوحى بـ is fine.

arabic: الطَّاوُوسُ البَلَدِيُّ مُنْتَشِرٌ فِي الجَنُوبِ، وَرِيشُهُ سُرُورٌ لِلْبَصَرِ.
english: The native peacock is common in the south, and its feathers are a pleasure to look at.
reason: 'الطاووس البلدي' as native peacock common in the south is dubious (peacocks aren't native to Arab regions), and the sentence reads like a forced pairing.

arabic: خَصَمَ البَنْكُ سَبْعِينَ مِلْيُونًا مِنْ ثَرْوَةِ الرَّجُلِ، فَغَيَّظَهُ ذَلِكَ.
english: The bank deducted seventy million from the man's wealth, and that made him angry.
reason: A bank 'deducting' seventy million from a man's wealth is an odd usage (ثروة isn't something banks deduct from); also غيّظه is unusual. Contrived.

arabic: صِنَاعَةُ الآلَاتِ تَطَوَّرَتْ فِي الكُوَيْتِ بَعْدَ أَنْ دَعَمَتْهَا الحُكُومَةُ.
english: The machine industry developed in Kuwait after the government supported it.

arabic: هَدَانَا الدَّلِيلُ فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ القَاسِيَةِ، فَنَجَوْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أَذًى.
english: The guide led us through the harsh desert, so we came through without any harm.
reason: Grammatical and coherent: the guide led us in the desert and we were safe; هدانا is slightly literary but fine.

arabic: عَبَأَ الوَلَدُ الأَسْمَرُ الكِيسَ بِمِضْرَبِهِ وَقَمِيصِهِ، ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ فِي طَرِيقِ الإِيَابِ.
english: The dark-haired boy packed his racket and shirt into the bag, then set off on the way back.
reason: 'الأسمر' means dark-skinned/brown, not 'dark-haired'; also 'packed the bag with his racket' is awkward (عبأ الكيس بـ) and مضرب is ambiguous.

arabic: نَظَّمَ المُصَوِّرُ مَجْمُوعَةً مِنْ صُوَرِهِ المُفَضَّلَةِ فِي دَفْتَرٍ وَفْقًا لِحَجْمِهَا.
english: The photographer organized a collection of his favorite photos in a notebook according to their size.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; photographer arranging photos by size.

arabic: فِي مَادَّةِ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ، أَدْرُسُ نُطْقَ حُرُوفِ الأَبْجَدِيَّةِ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ بِبُطْءٍ.
english: In the phonetics course, I slowly study the pronunciation of the letters of the English alphabet.
reason: Natural learner sentence about studying phonetics.

arabic: أَطْعَمَ الجَارُ كُلَّ جَوْعَانَ فِي الجِوَارِ عِجْلًا مَنْدِيًّا كَامِلًا فِي عِيدِ الأَضْحَى.
english: On Eid al-Adha, the neighbor fed every hungry person in the neighborhood a whole calf cooked mandi-style.
reason: Feeding every hungry person in the neighborhood a whole calf is implausible; also 'جوعان' with 'كل' is odd and 'عجلاً مندياً' is awkward.

arabic: دَامَ فَحْصُ تَأْشِيرَتِي إِلَى النِّرْوِيجِ سِتَّةَ أَشْهُرٍ، ثُمَّ أَعْلَمَتْنِي السِّفَارَةُ بِالقَبُولِ.
english: The review of my visa for Norway lasted six months, and then the embassy told me it had been accepted.
reason: Grammatical and plausible visa scenario.

arabic: أَلْقَى العَدُوُّ القَائِدَ فِي السِّجْنِ، لَكِنَّ النَّاسَ لَمْ يَتَجَاهَلُوا نَزَاهَتَهُ.
english: The enemy threw the leader into prison, but the people did not ignore his integrity.
reason: Coherent narrative sentence; grammatical.

arabic: بَعْدَ عَوْدَتِهِ إِلَى الرِّئَاسَةِ، قَادَ المُدِيرُ المُؤَسَّسَةَ بِجِدٍّ وَوَحَّدَ أَعْضَاءَهَا.
english: After his return to the presidency, the director led the institution with diligence and unified its members.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; formal news-style.

arabic: كَانَ أَبِي زَعْلَانَ، لَكِنَّ مِزَاجَهُ حَسُنَ بَعْدَ بُرْهَةٍ مِنَ المُسَلْسَلِ المُضْحِكِ.
english: My father was upset, but his mood improved after a while of watching the funny series.
reason: Natural, colloquial 'زعلان' mixed with MSA; plausible. Translation fine.

arabic: صَامَ النَّاسُ فِي الجِوَارِ بَعْدَ ظُهُورِ هِلَالِ الشَّهْرِ الهِجْرِيِّ التَّاسِعِ.
english: The people in the neighborhood fasted after the crescent of the ninth Hijri month appeared.
reason: Ramadan fasting after crescent sighting; correct.

arabic: اخْتَارَ الوَصِيفُ مُشْطًا جَدِيدًا وَمِقَصًّا لِلِحْيَتِهِ مِنْ دُكَّانِ الجَارِ.
english: The young man picked out a new comb and scissors for his beard at the neighbor's shop.
reason: 'الوصيف' means page/attendant/servant, not 'young man'; also 'مقصّ' is the standard form and 'مِقَصّ' is odd. Translation inaccurate.

arabic: البِذْلَةُ الحَدِيثَةُ لَمْ تُنَاسِبْنِي، فَأَعَدْتُ قِيَاسَهَا فِي الدُّكَّانِ مَعَ أَبِي.
english: The modern suit didn't fit me, so I had it measured again at the shop with my father.
reason: Plausible scenario; grammatical.

arabic: قَرَصَ السَّرَطَانُ الطِّفْلَ فَصَاحَ وَقَفَزَ، ثُمَّ عَانَقَتْهُ مَامَا وَدَاعَبَتْهُ.
english: The crab pinched the child, so he shouted and jumped, and then Mom hugged him and stroked him.
reason: Plausible scene; 'ماما' is colloquial but acceptable.

arabic: شَهِدَ هَذَا الصَّرْحُ اسْتِضَافَةَ مِهْرَجَانَاتٍ عَدِيدَةٍ فِي سَاحَتِهِ مُنْذُ قَرْنٍ.
english: For a century, this building has hosted many festivals in its square.
reason: Grammatical and plausible description of a landmark.

arabic: تَوَقَّعَ الضَّيْفُ مَنْسَفًا، لَكِنَّ المَائِدَةَ كَانَتْ خَاوِيَةً إِلَّا مِنَ المُقَبِّلَاتِ.
english: The guest expected mansaf, but the table was empty except for the appetizers.
reason: Coherent, natural scene; خاوية إلا من المقبلات is fine.

arabic: حَرَّكَتِ الأُمُّ خَلِيطَ البَهَارِ وَالنَّعْنَاعِ فِي الزَّبْدِيَّةِ المُسْتَدِيرَةِ، ثُمَّ جَعَلَتْهُ عَلَى المَائِدَةِ.
english: The mother stirred the mixture of spices and mint in the round bowl, then put it on the table.
reason: Plausible kitchen scene; grammatical. جعلته على المائدة is slightly unusual but acceptable.

arabic: عَالَجَ الخَبِيرُ أَلَمَ حَلْقِي فِي العِيَادَةِ بِالعِرْقِسُوسِ المَغْلِيِّ، وَكَانَ مُهَدِّئًا جِدًّا.
english: At the clinic, the expert treated my sore throat with boiled licorice, and it was very calming.
reason: An 'expert' treating a throat at a clinic is odd (should be doctor). Also 'ألم حلقي' is ungrammatical for 'my' (missing ya as possessive: حلقي is 'my throat', so 'ألم حلقي' means pain of my throat - fine), but the English says 'sore throat' and 'expert' for خبير, a poor fit; boiled licorice given by the clinic expert is forced.

arabic: تَحَرَّكَتْ عَضَلَةُ كَتِفِهِ تَدْرِيجِيًّا بَعْدَ الشِّفَاءِ، لَكِنَّهُ بَقِيَ مُتَثَاقِلًا.
english: His shoulder muscle gradually moved again after his recovery, but he stayed sluggish.
reason: Muscle 'moving gradually' then 'he stayed sluggish' is incoherent; متثاقلا doesn't fit the muscle/person link naturally.

arabic: كَنَسَتِ الشَّغَّالَةُ فَضَلَاتِ الهَمْسْتَرِ المَنْفُوشِ حَوْلَ صُنْدُوقِهِ وَهِيَ تُدَمْدِمُ.
english: The housekeeper swept up the fluffy hamster's droppings around its box, grumbling as she did.
reason: Forced word-list sentence: a housekeeper sweeping hamster droppings with 'fluffy' hamster is contrived; الشغالة is also colloquial and مفرد فضلات is awkward.

arabic: ظَهَرَ جُرَذٌ عِمْلَاقٌ فَظِيعٌ فِي التُّوَالِيتِ، فَهَتَفَتِ المَرْأَةُ مَذْعُورَةً.
english: A terrible giant rat appeared in the toilet, so the woman screamed in terror.

arabic: تَعْتَاشُ سُلَحْفَاتُنَا عَلَى الخَضْرَاوَاتِ وَالإِجَّاصِ، وَهِيَ مُولَعَةٌ بِالبَامْيَا جِدًّا.
english: Our tortoise lives on vegetables and pears, and she is very fond of okra.
reason: Natural pet tortoise sentence; grammatical, and 'lives on' fits تعتاش.

arabic: أَضَاءَ القِنْدِيلُ طَاقَ الكَاتِدْرَائِيَّةِ البِيزَنْطِيَّةِ، فَعَجِبَ الضَّيْفُ مِنْ بَهَائِهِ.
english: The lamp lit up the arch of the Byzantine cathedral, and the guest marveled at its splendor.
reason: Grammatical and plausible descriptive sentence, though طاق for arch and a lamp lighting it are fine.

arabic: فِي سُطُورِ هَذِهِ الأُسْطُورَةِ خَبِيئَةٌ وَلُغْزٌ، وَفِيهَا تَشْوِيقٌ لَا مَثِيلَ لَهُ.
english: Within the lines of this legend are a secret and a riddle, and it has suspense like nothing else.
reason: Catalog-like and forced: 'secret and riddle' in the lines of a legend with خبيئة is contrived word-list material.

arabic: جَارَتُنَا العَزْبَاءُ مَبْسُوطَةٌ جِدًّا بِنَظَّارَتِهَا الجَدِيدَةِ وَجِينْزِهَا الدَّاكِنِ الإِيطَالِيِّ.
english: Our single neighbor is very happy with her new eyeglasses and her dark Italian jeans.
reason: Colloquial-leaning but plausible and grammatical; translation accurate.

arabic: دَافَعَ الوَلَدُ عَنْ عِنَادِهِ، لَكِنَّ أُمَّهُ المُؤَنِّبَةَ جَعَلَتْهُ مُفْحَمًا.
english: The boy defended his stubbornness, but his scolding mother left him speechless.
reason: مفحما is passive-participle and المؤنبة as an epithet for the mother is awkward; 'defended his stubbornness' is contrived.

arabic: وَاظَبَ الطَّحَّانُ المُخَلِّصُ عَلَى الزِّرَاعَةِ، فَلَمْ تَمْنَعْهُ المَشَقَّةُ وَلَا التَّجَاعِيدُ.
english: The sincere miller kept at his farming, and neither hardship nor wrinkles stopped him.

arabic: أَوْشَكَتِ السَّفِينَةُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ الدَّوَّامَةَ، فَتَشَاوَرَ المُهَنْدِسَانِ الاثْنَانِ فَوْرًا.
english: The ship was about to enter the whirlpool, so the two engineers conferred immediately.
reason: Grammatical and coherent: أوشكت أن تدخل, engineers conferring.
